Vernetzt im Glauben: Wenn Religion zum Team-Spirit wird

Zwischen Konferenzräumen und Teamplakaten findet sich am Bonner Telekom-Campus ein Ort der Stille – der Silent Room. Darin: Gebetsteppiche, verschiedene Bibelausgaben und bald auch Bücher zum jüdischen Glauben. Dieser unscheinbare Ort ist Sinnbild dafür, was die Religions-Communities bei der Deutsche Telekom vereint: das gemeinsame Anliegen, ihren Glauben auch am Arbeitsplatz leben zu können – und damit Nähe und Verständnis füreinander zu schaffen. 

Am längsten etabliert in der Telekom ist die Community Christen@Telekom. Spokesperson Andrea Baare – von Haus aus promovierte evangelische Theologin – hat nach ihrem Studium den Weg zur Telekom gefunden. Sie betreut aktuell aus einer Vertriebsrolle heraus Vergabethemen für die bundesweiten Flughäfen in Deutschland. Ihr Wunsch: „Ich möchte nicht morgens zur Arbeit kommen und einen Teil meiner Persönlichkeit im Kofferraum lassen.“ So machte sie es sich gemeinsam mit der Community zur Aufgabe, Christinnen und Christen miteinander zu vernetzen und den Glauben im Arbeitsalltag zu leben. Zum Beispiel als Ansprechpartner in herausfordernden Situationen: „Trauerfälle und Verluste sind oft Themen, die für viele schwer anzusprechen sind.“ Gleichzeitig organisieren sie Adventsgottesdienste und Andachten, die nicht nur für Christinnen und Christen offenstehen. 

Amro Moussa schaut am liebsten auf das, was verbindet. Denn das ist deutlich stärker als das, was uns unterscheidet. Er ist Spokesperson der Community Salam@Telekom. Das Netzwerk sieht sich als unterstützendes Netzwerk für Mitarbeitende muslimischen Glaubens. „Unser Kernteam ist ein bunter Mix aus Persönlichkeiten, Berufen und Skills. Die Community besteht aus mehr als 10 Nationalitäten”, sagt Amro. Das Ziel von Salam@Telekom:  Das Netzwerk sensibilisiert, schafft Aufmerksamkeit und klärt auf – unter anderem durch das Feiern von Festen wie dem Fastenbrechen oder durch die Organisation von Spendenaktionen für wohltätige Zwecke.

Seit Herbst 2024 gibt es auch eine jüdische Gruppe: Shalom@Telekom. „Wir sind nicht nur eine Gruppe – wir sind ein lebendiges Beispiel für das Streben nach mehr Verständnis, mehr Akzeptanz und eine starke, inklusive Unternehmenskultur“, sagen die beiden Spokespersons Yaroslav Chepurniak und Daniel Friedmann. Der Employer Branding Manager aus Wien und der Data Scientist aus Bonn wollen ein Umfeld schaffen, in dem sich jüdische Mitarbeitende über Landesgrenzen hinweg sicher und unterstützt fühlen – sei es durch das Stärken der eigenen Identität, durch das Teilen von Traditionen oder die gemeinsame Verbundenheit mit Israel. Ihr Ziel ist, bei der gesamten Belegschaft der #Telekom das Bewusstsein für jüdische Traditionen und Werte zu erhöhen und durch Aufklärung Vorurteilen und Diskriminierung entgegenzuwirken.

Wichtig ist den Communities: Es geht darum, miteinander in Dialog zu treten. Und mit persönlichen Geschichten und gemeinsamen Werten Brücken zueinander zu bauen.

„Neurodiversity is beautiful“
 
Das steht auf dem Hoodie meiner Kollegin Sarah Lauer. Und sie lebt dieses Motto: offen, mutig und inspirierend.
 
Das manager magazin widmet sich in seiner aktuellen Ausgabe einem Thema, das mir persönlich und als Personalvorständin sehr am Herzen liegt: ADHS und Neurodiversität im Arbeitsleben. 👉 https://lnkd.in/excEuS35 (Bezahlschranke)
 
Menschen ticken unterschiedlich – und das ist ein Gewinn für Unternehmen. Und ich setze mich deshalb für ein Umfeld ein, in dem Vielfalt sichtbar wird und alle ihr volles Potenzial einbringen können.
 
Darum habe ich bei der Telekom die Schirmherrschaft für unsere Neurodiversity Community übernommen, die inzwischen über 700 Mitglieder zählt. Eine davon: Sarah Lauer. Sie trägt mit großem Engagement dazu bei, dass wir als Unternehmen Barrieren abbauen. Sei es im Rekruiting, im Arbeitsalltag oder in unseren Produkten.
 
Kolleginnen und Kollegen wie Sarah zeigen uns jeden Tag, wie wertvoll verschiedene Perspektiven für ein Unternehmen sind.
 
#Neurodiversity #Inclusion #Leadership

Ob sichtbar oder unsichtbar – jede Form von Diversität braucht Rahmenbedingungen, die Teilhabe ermöglichen. Denn auch physische Barrieren können ausschließen. Genau hier setzt das Netzwerk „Barrierefreie Software“ an. Vor über zehn Jahren gründeten Dagmar Wehr und Ralf Ossowski gemeinsam mit weiteren Kolleginnen und Kollegen das Netzwerk. Ihr Ziel: Barrierefreiheit im Unternehmen stärker bekannt machen und in die Entwicklungsprozesse verankern. Bis heute setzen sie sich aktiv für die Belange von Kolleg*innen mit Behinderungen ein.

Dagmar ist Experience Designerin #Accessibility. Sie erkannte früh, dass Usability, also Benutzerfreundlichkeit, und Barrierefreiheit zusammen betrachtet werden müssen. Denn Software, die für Nutzende ohne Einschränkungen gut funktioniert, bleibt für Menschen mit beispielsweise Hör- oder Sehbeeinträchtigungen oder mit motorischen Behinderungen oft unzugänglich. So können Menschen mit eingeschränkter Beweglichkeit Schwierigkeiten bei der Verwendung einer Maus oder Tastatur haben: Sie benötigen Software, die auf alternative Eingabemethoden wie Sprachsteuerung oder Augensteuerung ausgelegt ist.

Und auch Ralf erinnert sich, dass neue Software oft in den Tests zur Barrierefreiheit durchfiel. Um das zu ändern, schlug er intern vor, einen Support für die Themen Barrierefreiheit und Ergonomie zu etablieren. Der Erfolg trieb ihn an, das Thema im Konzern zu promoten und sich zu vernetzen. Heute arbeitet er selbst im Team Support Barrierefreiheit und Software-Ergonomie.

Die Mitglieder des Netzwerks werben für Barrierefreiheit und setzen sich dafür ein, dass bei Designfragen, Softwareentwicklungen und internen Schulungen immer die Bedürfnisse von Kolleg*innen mit Beeinträchtigungen mitberücksichtigt werden. Dabei geht es nicht nur um technische Lösungen, sondern auch um Sensibilisierung: „Wir müssen alle Beteiligten im Softwareentwicklungsprozess – angefangen vom Produkt Owner bis zur Testerin – für das Thema begeistern, damit es im Mindset der Menschen und somit im Unternehmen wirklich verankert wird“, erzählt Dagmar.

#Telekom #Barrierefreiheit

Wer in der Telekom „Einhorn Samantha“ oder „Ingo Flamingo“ sieht, weiß schnell: Hier sind die Maskottchen der #Neurodiversity Community unterwegs. Ob Autismus, ADHS oder Legasthenie – all das möchte die Community im Arbeitsumfeld sichtbar machen. Die Gründerinnen, Daniela Barmscheidt und Sarah Lauer, sind selbst neurodivergent. Beide hatten lange Zeit das Gefühl, damit in der #Telekom allein zu sein.

„Ich wollte eine Plattform, auf der wir uns austauschen und uns gegenseitig unterstützen können“, sagt Daniela. Sie arbeitet seit 2019 bei der Telekom Security in Leipzig. Sarah hat 2011 als IT-Studentin bei der Deutsche Telekom in Bonn begonnen.

Seit der Gründung ist die Community inzwischen auf über 700 Mitglieder angewachsen. Sie lebt davon, kleine „Kniffe“ und Lösungen zu teilen, die den Arbeitsalltag für neurodivergente Menschen erleichtern können. Ein Beispiel: Die Mittagspause in der Kantine kann für viele eine enorme Herausforderung darstellen – der Lärm, die Hektik und die vielen Menschen sind überwältigend. Der Tipp: nicht zur Stoßzeit gehen oder sich gemeinsam etwas holen und dann woanders essen. Auch die Vorbereitung auf Meetings ist ein Thema: eine vorab verschickte Agenda kann für neurodivergente Mitarbeitende von unschätzbarem Wert sein, um sich ausreichend vorzubereiten.

The more digital we become, the louder the fear: is #HR losing its human touch? 👥
 
At yesterday’s 6th #CHRO Roundtable by Mercer and German association for Personnel management (DGFP) in Frankfurt, I argued the opposite.
 
HR in #responsibility means exactly that:
 
✔️ Digital and human-centric HR are not a contradiction. They’re a choice.
 
🧠The real shift? Moving HR from transactional to strategic. Less time on routine queries, admin, and process work, more time on leadership conversations, capability building, and the cultural change that only humans can drive. Vice versa: Where humans are irreplaceable, the bar must be raised, not maintained.
 
And the most important lever? #Upskilling. Not as a training program, but as a strategic bet on human potential. We can’t predict which roles will exist in 5 years. But we can build organizations that are ready to adapt. That’s HR’s job now.

This week, I spent dedicated time with my leadership team to focus on team effectiveness. 🤝

In the daily pace of leadership, it’s easy to stay in execution mode, focused on results and decisions. But high-performing teams also need to pause, reflect, and recalibrate how they work together. Especially since our team has evolved, with new perspectives, shifting roles, and changing priorities. 

One topic that stood out in our discussions was the balance between two perspectives we all carry as leaders:
 ➡️ the “organization hat,” where we think and act for the overall HR organization, and
 ➡️ the “interaction hat,” where we represent our own pillar, bringing functional depth and having our teams in mind.

Switching between these two is not always easy. In the moment, it can shape how we frame arguments, make decisions, and engage with each other. What helped us was making this explicit and being transparent about which “hat” we are wearing when we contribute to a discussion. This simple shift creates clarity, reduces friction, and strengthens trust within the team.

Another powerful metaphor we used was the german word “Haltung”: taking a moment to pause (“Halt”), reflect on our own behavior and mindset, and then consciously move into action (“Tun”) in the discussion.

Grateful for the openness and honesty in the room – these moments aren’t always easy, but they’re essential to lead with impact. 🙏

#Leadership #TeamEffectiveness #Reflection

🚀 A proud next step for AI pioneering at Infineon HR 🚀

Yesterday, we marked an important step in our HR transformation journey with the pilot launch of our first Agentic AI use case in MyHR.

This is much more than a new feature — it’s a test‑and‑learn moment for us. We deliberately started with a non‑mission‑critical, repetitive use case so we can safely experiment, gather insights, and apply our learnings to the next Agentic AI solutions already in the pipeline.

Our first pilot use case helps to intelligently re-route HR tickets to the correct HR teams — saving a few minutes per case and supporting a faster, more customer‑centric HR experience.
To ensure quality and trust, we’ve implemented a confidence-based approach:
If the AI is over 90% confident, it processes the case end‑to‑end.
If confidence drops below that, a human colleague steps in to make the final decision.

This is where human and artificial intelligence come together — a perfect interplay of automation and human judgment to deliver meaningful impact.

A huge thank you to all colleagues from HR and IT who are part of this journey. Your curiosity, collaboration, and drive to explore new ways of working make innovation like this possible.

And this is only the beginning. We will continue to iterate, improve, and scale further Agentic AI use cases as we learn.

Transformation braucht einen starken Industriestandort. Genau darüber haben wir gestern bei der Chemie³-Dialogveranstaltung „Standort unter Druck“ in Berlin intensiv gesprochen. Die Diskussion zeigt: Die chemisch-pharmazeutische Industrie steht mitten in einem tiefgreifenden Wandel – unter schwierigen geopolitischen und wirtschaftlichen Rahmenbedingungen.

Die Transformation ist ein harter Stresstest für unsere Branche, gerade angesichts der geopolitischen Krisen und der großen Herausforderungen am Standort Deutschland. Aber unser Land hat mit seinem Know-how und seinen Fachkräften große Potenziale, die uns im internationalen Wettbewerb Vorteile verschaffen. Wir müssen mit strukturellen Reformen dafür sorgen, dass uns hohe Kosten für Energie, Arbeit und Bürokratie nicht länger ausbremsen. Nur wenn wir Wettbewerbsfähigkeit zurückgewinnen, können wir Arbeitsplätze in der Branche halten und unseren Beitrag zu ökologischen Zielen wie CO2-Reduktion oder Kreislaufwirtschaft leisten.

Mit Chemie³ bringen wir als Chemie-Arbeitgeber gemeinsam mit unseren Partnern unterschiedliche Perspektiven zusammen und arbeiten an tragfähigen Lösungen. Genau dieses Zusammenspiel brauchen wir jetzt – für unsere Branche und den Standort Deutschland.

Mein Dank gilt ☀️ Katie Gallus für die Moderation sowie Claudia Major, Christian Moser, Mona Neubaur, Markus Steilemann, Heike Vesper, Michael Vassiliadis, Michael Hüther und Anke Rehlinger für die engagierte und differenzierte Diskussion. Ebenso danke ich allen Mitwirkenden und Teilnehmenden für den offenen Austausch und die wichtigen Impulse.

Heute fand die größte und anspruchsvollste Sicherheitsübung an unserem BASF-Standort Ludwigshafen statt: die jährliche Großschadensalarmübung! 🚒

Gemeinsam mit externen Einsatzkräften trainierten unsere Gefahrenabwehreinheiten ein realistisches Szenario mit einer Verpuffung mit Folgebrand und mehreren verletzten Personen. Zum Glück nur eine Übung. Doch genau solche Übungen stellen sicher, dass wir auf den Ernstfall vorbereitet sind.
 
Sicherheit ist für BASF kein „Nebenbei“-Thema, sondern die Grundlage unseres Handelns. Deshalb investieren wir nicht nur in moderne Technik, sondern auch in kontinuierliches Training und gemeinsames Lernen. Am meisten beeindruckt hat mich heute die enge Zusammenarbeit aller internen und externen Beteiligten. Das hat einmal mehr gezeigt, was möglich ist, wenn Erfahrung, Vertrauen und Professionalität zusammenkommen. Sicherheit ist Teamarbeit. Genau dieses Miteinander macht den Unterschied, wenn es darauf ankommt.
 
Mein herzlicher Dank gilt allen, die diese Übung mit großem Engagement vorbereitet und durchgeführt haben – insbesondere unseren Einsatzkräften. Sie übernehmen täglich Verantwortung für die Sicherheit am Standort und leisten damit einen unverzichtbaren Beitrag für unsere Mitarbeitenden, unsere Nachbarschaft und unsere Umwelt. Und das verdient höchste Anerkennung!

Mental health is an essential part of our well-being. It shapes our private and work life and the challenges arising from it are increasing globally. An estimated 15% of working-age adults are having a mental disorder.  

What concerns me most is the invisible burden many employees carry silently — stress, burnout, and anxiety that often go unnoticed until it’s too late. To speak up and talk about mental health and to raise awareness are important first steps to prevent this.  

At BASF, we’re working on creating a culture where these conversations can happen more openly — and where support for mental health is part of how we lead. Because mental and emotional health is critical to both our employees and the company.  

Leaders have a crucial role in creating that sort of environment by fostering trust, noticing early signs, and responding with empathy and accountability. That’s why we have already launched the Mental Health Alliance and the eleMENTAL platform, offering verified information, learning materials, events, and local contacts for all employees and leaders, accessible in multiple languages and across all devices. Our goal is to empower everyone to proactively care for their mental health and to break down stigma.  

I am personally committed to fostering a culture where seeking help is seen as a sign of strength, not weakness. Let’s work together to make mental health support accessible and visible for all.

A groundbreaking is always a statement of belief -
in a place, in its people, and in the future.

Last week, we made such a statement by breaking ground on our new Siemens Energy switchgear factory in Mississippi. The site will create up to 300 advanced manufacturing jobs and include a dedicated training center to help build the skills we need today - and tomorrow.

This matters because U.S. electricity demand keeps rising, currently by about 2 percent each year. That may sound modest. But it means adding the power demand of roughly eight million homes annually.

Meeting that demand will require stronger, more resilient grid infrastructure – including state-of-the-art switchgear.

Thank you to everyone who helped make this investment possible. The future of energy depends on a stronger grid - and we're building it!

Worth reading! The Financial Times highlights an important reality in its latest deep dive on transformers: the race to build AI infrastructure is no longer just about chips, software or data centers; it's also about the grid infrastructure that powers them.

Large power transformers have become one of the most critical pieces of that infrastructure. At Siemens Energy, we're investing responsibly and sustainably in capacity expansions around the globe to meet the growing demand.👇

2026 has shown how much pressure energy systems are under - from geopolitics, and supply chain disruptions to increasingly volatile demand patterns. Which brings us to a key question: How can we build energy systems that withstand these new stress levels?

This is at the heart of today’s Siemens Energy Customer Experience Days in Berlin, where about 230 decision-makers have come together. When discussing how to increase resilience in a far more volatile world, one theme keeps coming up: structural shifts.

👉 From predictable to volatile, dynamic loads
👉 From technology focus to system thinking
👉 From traditional customer roles to deep partnerships as co-creators

That shows: Resilience is not only about individual assets. It’s about how fast we can connect, integrate, and scale entire systems. Systems that we design together with our customers from day one.

Thank you to all customers, partners and colleagues from #TeamPurple who made this event such an inspiring experience!

The energy transition is more than just adding renewable generation. It’s about building systems that are secure, reliable, affordable and sustainable.

In this context, the expansion of offshore grid connections is one of the most demanding tasks we face today. Especially at the speed now needed.

That’s why I’m pleased that we’ve been awarded the grid project ‘North Sea Connector 2’ – together with strong partners across the maritime value chain.

Up to 2 gigawatts of offshore wind energy will be transmitted reliably to shore. And around 95% of the value added by Siemens Energy happens in Germany: The transformers and converters will come from Nuremberg, the SF₆-free, gas-insulated switchgear from Berlin.

Projects like this show what energy security and the transition at scale require:
👉 advanced grid technology
👉 industrial capacity
👉 strong partnerships

This way, we strengthen resilience, reduce dependencies, and secure reliable power for the future. And: it shows that Germany has the capabilities to deliver.

#OffshoreWind #Grids #MadeInGermany

Electricity demand is exploding – and the grid is the foundation to meet it.

At this year’s Atlantic Council Global Energy Forum, one point stood out: Energy affordability will be determined by how fast we build and modernize power infrastructure. Today, we’re seeing that a lot of capacity exists, but can’t connect. In addition, aging grids are stretched beyond limits and their original design. Consequently, costs rise because infrastructure lags.

That’s why we must shift:
 ⚡ From discussing single solutions to system thinking.
 ⚡ From bespoke products to standardized build-out.
 ⚡ From sequential to parallel execution.

At Siemens Energy, our focus is: unlock capacity now, e.g. with digital grid solutions. And scale the grid long term, e.g. by ramping up our manufacturing footprint globally. In the US alone, we invest $1 billion, creating more than 1,500 highly skilled jobs.

And yes - AI will play a role. Not just in driving demand, but in making grids smarter and more efficient. That’s why we continuously expand our AI capabilities, such as with our Grid AI Lab in Orlando, the announced acquisition of Camlin Group, or with new partnerships.

In the end, it’s not only about building more power. It’s about building a system that works together efficiently, effectively and intelligently. That’s what ultimately makes energy affordable.

Thanks for the great discussion Sherri Goodman, Alex Fitzsimmons, Josh Parker, Bonnie Titone!

#ACEnergyForum #GEF2026

Artificial intelligence is driving electricity demand – but it will also help solve the challenges it creates.
 
Coming back from this year’s #DatacloudGlobalCongress in Cannes, I was pleased to see that industry is not short of ideas on how to solve the power density challenge for data centers.
 
➡️ Demand is growing fast: By 2030, data centers may consume more electricity than Japan. 
 ➡️ Yet, around 20% of planned data center projects globally are at risk due to grid constraints.
➡️ That means: We don’t just need more generation capacity. We also need better end-to-end coordination, and more focus on the grid.
 
And that’s where #AI changes the game: By making our technologies more intelligent, we optimize power flows, assets and forecasting. That unlocks additional #grid capacity.
 
At Siemens Energy, we expand our AI capabilities accordingly: In April, we opened the first Grid AI Lab. This week, we announced the agreement to acquire Camlin Group, a specialist in grid monitoring, analytics and asset digitalization technologies. In addition, at #DCGC, we announced to support NVIDIA DSX, improving end-to-end power architectures, from grid to chip.
 
Because in the end, it’s about building a system that works together.

As data becomes the operating system of the grid, we’re advancing where it matters most.

Three foundation stone layings. Two countries. One signal: Europe’s energy security is being built now.

From Austria to Croatia, this week we laid the groundwork to strengthen today's grid - and build tomorrow's.

Europe has more installed renewable capacity than ever before. But much of this cannot be fully used or connected. Per year, the continent is wasting over 70 TWh of renewable electricity by being curtailed due to grid bottlenecks. That’s nearly Austria’s annual electricity use.

And the roadblocks don’t stop there: Around 1.7 TW of new planned renewable projects are stuck waiting for grid connections across Europe. That’s almost as much as China’s total installed renewable capacity.
Unlike China, in Europe we’re not building generation and grids side by side. That makes the grid infrastructure one of Europe’s biggest energy challenges.

If we want true energy transition, resilience, and sovereignty, we must break down these grid bottlenecks – through better planning, more investments, and effective tenders, just to name a few.

At the sidelines of #WindEurope2026, at a joint event with TenneT, we’ve committed to build more renewable energy – and bring more of it online. Thank you to everyone pushing for real change, in this case especially to Ina Kamps and Hauke Jürgensen🙏

As an AI enthusiast, grid technologist, and Florida resident, this one feels special. Yesterday, we opened our first Siemens Energy Grid AI Lab in Orlando, focused on one of the biggest challenges of our time: modernizing and future‑proofing our electricity #grids.

We celebrated this huge step together with Mayor Buddy Dyer, our Head of Digital Grid Adnan Chaudhry, key partners like NVIDIA, SoftServe and World Wide Technology, customers, as well as colleagues – all aligned around the mission of making the grid ready for the future.

A future that is already here: extreme weather, aging infrastructure, rising system complexity, cyber risks, and rapidly growing electricity demand — especially from AI. By 2030, data‑center power demand alone could double, adding the equivalent of a Japan‑sized load to the grid.

However, AI is not only one of the many challenges – it's also part of the solution. That’s why our new lab connects advanced AI infrastructure with deep grid expertise. Our goal is to turn product, system and environmental data into real intelligence, enabling power grids to shift from reactive to predictive.

Big thanks to everyone who helped bring this lab to life. It’s an important milestone, and after launching our new digital grid portfolio #Noedra, another signal of how seriously we take the role of digital and #AI solutions in our grid infrastructure.

⚡️ Securing Europe’s Energy Future: Why Grid Stability in the North & Baltic Seas Matters 🌊

The North and Baltic Seas have long powered Europe’s prosperity. Now, they’re taking center stage in our clean energy transition — set to become the beating heart of Europe’s renewable ambitions.

With North Sea Energy Cooperation (NSEC) nations targeting a combined 120 GW of offshore wind by 2030, and Baltic states preparing grids for up to 93 GW, the challenge isn’t just generating green electricity — it’s delivering it reliably across the continent.

The solution? Modern, interconnected grids and advanced digitalization. Cross-sea interconnectors enable real-time energy sharing, boost resilience, and help balance supply and demand. Critical technologies like synchronous condensers keep frequency stable as renewables grow, ensuring the lights stay on even when the wind varies.

At Siemens Energy, we have the technology and commitment to build a clean, secure, and resilient energy future for generations to come. But to unlock offshore wind’s full potential, we need all hands on deck: governments, industry, and communities need to accelerate interconnector projects, invest in digital and cyber resilience, and streamline regulation.

This week’s #EnergyIslandSummit2025 marked a historic step in that direction, as the pioneering Bornholm Energy Island has received green light. This first hybrid energy island will link Denmark and Germany using shared infrastructure and multi-terminal HVDC technology. With this, Europe is starting to harness the vast opportunities of the North and Baltic Seas — not only as energy sources, but also as the foundation of a cleaner, more secure, and resilient continent. 

#GridStability #EnergySecurity

Geopolitics, economic volatility, shifting regulation, AI moving fast. Pressure is building on organisations from several directions at once. For HR, helping the business transform is one task. Transforming ourselves to manage these changes is where it gets real.

This task set the tone for our recent HR All Hands Offsite, where our global HR community focused on three areas: how we develop our leaders, how we work with AI, and how we run the function.

When used well, AI makes HR more human, not less. The move that matters is embedding it where the work already happens. As automations take on more of the complex, multi-step tasks, our people can spend more of their time on what technology cannot do: being present, building trust, and being a real human interface to the business.

That's why leadership itself sits at the centre. The job is no longer to keep things steady. It is to grow people who hold a clear direction while their surroundings shift, and to turn our executive programmes into everyday practice.

The same honesty has to apply to how we run the function. The real gain comes from doing things once and well, as one team, and that takes leaders willing to question how we work.

The strongest moments came from learning across the organisation. Our teams shared openly and built on each other. That is #TeamRWE at its best.

Thank you to everyone who contributed and continues to shape the future of HR at RWE.

My position as an Executive Board Member changes every conversation before a word is said. Something which is rarely discussed among top management is that truly honest feedback becomes scarce.

Dissent is phrased more cautiously, feedback loses its sharp edges, and much of what really needs to be expressed remains unsaid. Yet leaders have to be able to rely on people in their own circle who are trustworthy and unaffected by hierarchical differences. And these people, in turn, need an environment where they feel safe and valued.

I greatly value those around me who, despite my role, continue to treat me with clarity and honesty. Today, when I seek advice, I turn to colleagues who approach me with integrity and tell me what they think, regardless of whether or not it's pleasant for me personally. I also seek out conversations with those whose perspectives challenge me, sometimes from angles I wouldn't have considered on my own. They encourage me to re-examine my own take on things, even when I felt certain about it beforehand.

I wasn't born a board member. For most of my career, I sat on the other side of the table. And that’s why I know from personal experience the impact a leadership position can have on others. We must consistently act with courage, steadfastness, and clarity in our interactions with each other!

Current debate keeps asking whether AI is a job killer or an engine for growth. From where I sit, it is neither. It is a leadership and organisational stress test – and how we shape it is on us.
 
That was the question our panel at the Allianz der Chancen network meeting in Düsseldorf discussed. Together with representatives from research, business, the political sphere and unions, we looked at how AI is reshaping work, what it means for skills and continuous training, and how transitions can be designed in a socially sustainable way. The decisive variable is not the technology but rather how we lead.
 
One thing is clear: AI does not replace human judgement, it actually raises the need for it. The skills that are gaining in importance are the human ones – critical thinking, leadership and collaboration.
 
This is where business, unions and policy-makers must deliver together by creating room for experimentation, incentivising scaling, investing with focus, and enabling employee participation.
 
Thank you to Nina Weigel for guiding us through the discussion so well, to my fellow panellists Ronald Bachmann, Johannes Pöttering, Jochen Ott and Knut Giesler for the good discussion, and to Andreas Schmitz, Dr. Ariane Reinhart  and the team at Allianz der Chancen for hosting.

Why do I keep going on pilgrimage year after year?
 
People walk the Camino de Santiago for many reasons. Some are fulfilling a lifelong dream, whilst others walk for spiritual reasons, to recover from an illness or to come to terms with the loss of a loved one.

For me, it is also an endeavour where the journey is the destination. It has become a personal tradition that during springtime I walk a stretch of it. This year I covered 175 kilometres from La Romieu to Argagnon in France on the Via Podiensis. I cherish these days of being in beautiful nature all day, without meetings nor screens, when my mind can settle, and my body finds the soothing rhythm of the trail.
 
What I find there is something that everyday life rarely affords me: genuine time to reflect, to recharge my batteries and to draw strength. The daily 5 to 7-hour walks carry an element of resilience too. Everyone walks at their own pace and meets their own personal limits. Nothing else allows me to do this in quite the same way.
 
I also cherish the exchange with like-minded pilgrims from all over the world, whom you meet on the trail or over dinner in the lodgings – this year Canadians, Australians, Scots, Israelis, Swiss and Dutch. Despite our different paths and backgrounds, we share the same beautiful experience and many a good conversation.
 
I'm returning to my desk with (let's be honest) slightly tired legs but energised with a fresh and clear mind. Whilst I'm already looking forward to next year's stage over the Pyrenees, the impressions of the last few days will stay with me for quite some time. 🥾

The recipe matters more than the kitchen.
 
That is the title and the central finding of the first paper published by our RWE Commercial AI Lab in Bellevue, Washington State. It argues that in AI weather prediction, how you train a model – the data it learns from, the methods used, what it is rewarded for getting right – matters at least as much as the design of the model itself.
 
The initial findings from our AI Lab are quite something, as they offer direct business value. Better weather prediction means sharper trading decisions, smarter dispatch of renewable assets, and stronger resilience when extremes hit the grid.
 
My sincere thanks to the four authors of the paper: Piyush Garg, Diana Gergel, and Galen Yacalis from our Commercial AI Lab, as well as Andrew Shao, PhD from Hewlett Packard Enterprise. You brought the recipe to the kitchen!
 
Why this matters beyond academia:
 
▪︎ NVIDIA Earth-2 Open Models (FCN3, Atlas) and ECMWF’s AIFS-Ens ranked higher than other models in the overall model assessment. However, no single model performed consistently across all the metrics, thus suggesting that the choice of training pipeline matters more than choosing the right architecture.
▪︎ The study's impact is already resonating within academic institutions and wider groups working on building AI weather models. NVIDIA teams have reached out directly.
▪︎ Using NVIDIA Earth2Studio – the open framework now standard for testing AI weather models – the team validated the results across ten architectures, thirty initialisation dates and four extreme events – the 2021 Pacific Northwest heat dome, the Texas freeze, Winter Storm Elliott and the 2023 heatwave in Europe.
 
What I find most compelling is how this work positions RWE and our research team at the AI Lab as a contributor to the science the AI field depends on. The energy transition runs on forecasts and some of the science behind them is now being shaped at RWE.

AI for value. Humans at the centre. Real impact only happens when AI is truly embedded into everyday work – not as a concept, but as part of how decisions are made, processes run, and teams collaborate.
 
Last week at the Government Innovation Board hosted by GovTech Deutschland, I shared how we at RWE are working with AI, particularly in the context of agentic AI.
 
Four key messages shaped my speech:
 
▪︎ The division of labour is shifting, but the human stays at the centre: Agentic systems prepare tasks, weigh up options and flag where action is needed – always within clear guardrails. Speed, structuring and pattern recognition move to the system. Judgement and decision-making authority remain with people.
▪︎ Real innovation happens in concrete workflows – where processes are genuinely understood and responsibility is lived.
▪︎ Governance builds trust and resilience: AI governance is not optional – it is the foundation for safe, transparent and responsible AI use at scale.
▪︎ AI challenges leadership: leaders must become role models in learning and using AI. Change management is crucial for a successful AI transformation.
 
One thing became clear once again: public administration and industry are working towards a shared agenda – building capabilities, strengthening trust, and scaling AI responsibly – even if at different stages.
 
Many thanks to Markus Richter and Achim Berg for the invitation and dialogue, and to Bernd Gemein for sharing the Deutsche Post perspective.

Leadership has never been about certainty; it has much rather been about helping others move forward without it.
 
End of last week, over 170 colleagues from near and far gathered in Copenhagen for our 7th RWE Group Leadership Meeting. What made this year’s meeting truly special to me was the collective energy in the room which was filled with a sense of purpose, determination and vision. 
 
This year’s theme: Living Leadership. This was chosen because we’re currently witnessing three profound shifts happening simultaneously:

▪︎ Speed and complexity: We are scaling our portfolio, our partnerships and our geographies at pace. Decisions must be driven by competitive outcomes, not by waiting for perfect information, which in the current environment is rarely available.
▪︎ Technology and AI: AI is transforming the tools available to us, creating new opportunities but also uncertainties around accountability, skills, and where human judgement ends and the algorithm begins. AI is not an IT initiative. It is a leadership topic that is relevant to every one of us.
▪︎ Permanent transformation: Change is no longer a phase. It is the operating condition. In this world, resilience is not a soft skill; it is an organisational capability. And the instinct to control complexity can become a liability. Leadership is about creating clarity and adaptability under pressure.

In practice, Living Leadership comes down to the following factors: being explicit about priorities and trade-offs; owning decisions even when AI has shaped the analysis; building teams that are empowered enough to act and where it is safe enough to speak up. But it is also our personal responsibility – leading others requires a strong self. We as leaders need to be fit for future, confident, curious, and capable of performing in this uncompromised environment.  

That is how resilience is built – not through comfort, but through capability.
 
Thank you to everyone involved for two days of clear thinking and meaningful conversations.

Industrial history and personal history are rarely far apart. That connection became very real when 91-year-old Paul Diestelhorst opened his photo albums and gave us a glimpse into a life shaped by the power station in Frimmersdorf. A rare and valuable insight.
 
The demolition of cooling tower Q at the end of February made the connection very tangible. The enormous steel and concrete chimney was built in the 1960s as part of what would become Europe's largest power station at that time. It is a significant part of our company's history and of the region's industrial identity.
 
At the age of 19, Paul came to Frimmersdorf in search of work. What followed was an entire working life with RWE – from power plant operator to control room operator to foreman. He knew every corner of tower Q. And at this advanced age, he witnessed the demolition of the very structure that he helped build and operate for decades.
 
Stories like Paul’s demonstrate to me what makes RWE stand out as an employer: the recognition of every single employee’s contribution. Day in, day out, shift after shift, on land and at sea.
 
With RWE’s accelerated phase-out of coal by 2030, a chapter of industrial history is coming to an end. And at the same time, our story continues. The Frimmersdorf site, for example, will be transformed into an innovative digital and transformation hub, and key parts of the power station will be preserved in the spirit of industrial heritage conservation. That is what RWE stands for: knowing and respecting our history yet always looking ahead and shaping the future.
 
Thank you, Paul, for everything you have achieved and given to #TeamRWE.

Cybersecurity is a top priority for RWE. After all, cyberattacks on critical infrastructure are no longer the exception – they are part of our everyday reality.

Yesterday, I spoke about precisely this topic at the Digitalk meets ZACTALK event (Digitale Stadt Düsseldorf e.V.) at XPONENTIAL Europe and highlighted three key perspectives:

▪︎ Cybersecurity is a key factor in building trust: for our employees, for our partners and for society, which relies on a reliable energy supply at all times.
▪︎ Cybersecurity as a strategic issue: cybersecurity is managed just like any other key management and risk issue: transparently, taking a risk-aware approach and an integrated view of resilience.
▪︎ The corporate culture dimension: sustainable cybersecurity is effective not only in systems, but also in day-to-day actions and through mindset. It requires informed, attentive, and empowered employees and managers who actively exemplify security. At RWE, we bring this to life through a variety of formats – from web-based trainings and phishing simulations to live hacking sessions and escape rooms.

AI is a particular focus. It is fundamentally changing the risk landscape, including in the field of cybercrime. Precisely because AI-powered cyberattacks specifically target the human factor, human judgement becomes more important – not less so.

For RWE, this means that cybersecurity does not end with prevention. Strong detection and response capabilities, clear responsibilities and a security culture that is put into practice form the foundation for a secure energy transition without disruption.

It is not every day that industry, law enforcement and the military sit down together to discuss security and economic policy perspectives. Thank you for this enriching discussion Manfred Boudreaux-Dehmer, Markus Hartmann, Jens Elstermeier and Stephan Schneider for chairing.

Creating these opportunities across business units is essential for us. Development happens when curiosity meets real responsibility. And transformation succeeds when people are given the space to explore, learn and grow.

Because in the end, the energy transition is powered by people.

Warum will niemand mehr Führungskraft werden?

Das wollte DER SPIEGEL von Heike Bruch wissen. Sie ist die Herausgeberin der St. Galler Jugendstudie, die drei Kipppunkte ausgemacht hat, wieso junge Menschen keine Lust mehr auf Führungspositionen haben.

Vorgesetzte wirken oft ausgebrannt und in einer Arbeitsmühle, die wenig erfüllend wirkt. Junge Menschen nehmen Strukturen als alt und starr wahr. Und: Führungskräfte spüren oft eine Überforderung oder das Gefühl, am Limit zu arbeiten, sodass sie ihre Führungsaufgaben am liebsten wieder abgeben möchten.

Die Quintessenz – und auch mein Erleben aus meinem beruflichen Alltag: Es fehlt dem Nachwuchs nicht an Ehrgeiz, sondern mitunter an Möglichkeiten, Verantwortung zu erproben, und auch an Vorbildern, die zeigen: So sieht gute Führung aus. So macht Führung Spaß.

Wir bei RWE sind uns unserer Verantwortung, Führungskräfte kontinuierlich auszubilden, bewusst. Zunächst einmal ist es sicherlich erfreulich, dass wir bei RWE keinen Mangel an Mitarbeitenden haben, die Führungsaufgaben übernehmen möchten. Nun liegt es an uns, eine Umgebung zu schaffen, die sich von der oben skizzierten deutlich unterscheidet. Dazu zählt, dass wir unsere Führungskräfte und Potenzialträger auf ihrer Reise begleiten und unterstützen.

Für den Gesamtkonzern haben wir unser Führungskräfteprogramm, unsere RWE Executive Journey, weiter geschärft. In Linie mit unserem Purpose, unseren Unternehmenswerten und unseren erfolgskritischen Verhaltensweisen haben wir ein gemeinsames Führungsverständnis definiert: Unsere RWE Leadership Principles. Diese Führungsprinzipien folgen klaren Standards und formulieren eine klare Erwartung, wie gute Führung bei RWE gelebt wird:

▪︎ Lead for Business Impact
▪︎ Lead to Deliver
▪︎ Lead for Team Success

Eine Umgebung zu schaffen, in der unsere Mitarbeitenden am besten wachsen und wirken können, liegt an uns. Wir begleiten unsere Führungskräfte auf jedem Schritt ihrer Reise und bereiten sie strukturiert auf ihre Rolle vor. Das gilt für das gesamte Spektrum von der ersten Führungsrolle, der Weiterentwicklung als Führungskraft oder einem Neueinstieg bis zum Gesellschaftswechsel.

Wichtig ist uns auch: Leadership ist nicht immer eine lineare Entwicklung, sondern hochindividuell: Es gibt auch Möglichkeiten zurück in Fachpositionen, geteilte Führungsrollen oder Sabbaticals als Möglichkeiten, neue Perspektiven kennenzulernen.

Unsere RWE Executive Journey unterstützt kontinuierlich, leitet an und ermutigt, den Schritt in die Führungsverantwortung zu gehen. Ein großer Dank an die vielen HR Kolleginnen und Kollegen aus dem gesamten Konzern, die gemeinsam RWEs Weg an dieser Stelle unterstützen.

Ich bin schon sehr gespannt, wie sich die Ergebnisse in unserem Unternehmen widerspiegeln werden. Denn ich bin überzeugt: Führung ist attraktiv!

What does leadership look like when the world feels unpredictable? 
 
That was the focus of our discussions at this year’s Global Women’s Network Conference #GWN, where I had the privilege of sharing the stage with our Offshore Wind CFO Gunhild Grieve. How urgent this question is, shows the current situation in the Middle East. Energy markets can shift in an instant while assets last for decades. Leading teams in this environment requires clear direction, curiosity, and teamwork. It also takes courage — the courage to be open, show vulnerability, and face uncertainty together. Listening to different perspectives and sharing my own, I reflected on the small actions that help people feel supported and confident even when everything else is in motion. 
 
During these moments in a BANI world, our values and Essential Behaviours provide anchors. Leadership is about conviction. Conviction means being stable in purpose but flexible in method. You adjust how you move, but not why you move. And that stability helps people feel grounded, especially when change is constant. 
 
Sharing stories and ideas in this space reminded me that leadership isn’t only about decisions. It’s about people, culture, and the everyday actions that help us navigate change together. Moments like these leave me grateful and excited to continue learning and growing alongside such an incredible network of colleagues.

21 % der Schülerinnen und Schüler in Deutschland leben in Armut oder sind armutsgefährdet. Fast eine halbe Million Schülerinnen und Schüler benötigen schulische Unterstützung, können sich diese aber nicht leisten. Wir helfen mit, dagegen zu steuern. Seit April 2025 unterstützt die RWE Foundation den Lern-Fair e.V durch ein Mitarbeiterpartizipationsprojekt. 
 
Lern-Fair ist eine Plattform, die Kindern, Jugendlichen und jungen Erwachsenen in Ausbildung aus herausfordernden Lebenslagen kostenlose digitale Lernunterstützung ermöglicht. Gleichzeitig ermöglicht Lern-Fair ein barrierearmes, flexibles Ehrenamt - ortsunabhängig und inklusiv - sodass auch Menschen mit Behinderung oder eingeschränkter Mobilität aktiv mitwirken können. Das Angebot geht von Hausaufgabenhilfe, über Prüfungsvorbereitung bis hin zu Kursen zur Förderung der ganzheitlichen Entwicklung. Ziel ist es, die schulischen Leistungen zu verbessern, damit die Chancen auf höhere Bildungsabschlüsse zu steigern und gleichzeitig das Selbstvertrauen und die Motivation der Kinder und Jugendlichen zu stärken. Soziales Engagement gehört bei RWE zur Unternehmenskultur. Mit dieser Partnerschaft wollen wir ganz konkret dazu beitragen, dass mehr Kinder und Jugendliche faire Bildungschancen bekommen. Und weil junge Menschen ihre Startbedingungen nicht beeinflussen können, sollten wir uns dafür einsetzen, allen eine faire Chance zu ermöglichen. Schlussendlich profitieren wir alle davon – als Gesellschaft, aber auch ganz persönlich. Unser RWE-Kollege Christopher Savage ist ein starkes Beispiel dafür, dass das Engagement für Lern-Fair nicht nur den Nachwuchs bereichert, sondern auch die Ehrenamtlichen selbst.
 
Ich bin stolz darauf, dass sich bereits so viele Kolleginnen und Kollegen aus dem #TeamRWE auf vielfältige Art und Weise sozial engagieren. Gemeinsam machen wir den Unterschied!

Bleiben wir Anwender oder ist unser Anspruch bei KI ein anderer?
 
Unter anderem darum ging es bei „Allianz der Chancen trifft… Lars Klingbeil“ gestern in Berlin. Die Arbeitswelt geht in die nächste Phase über. Und die gelingt nur im Zusammenspiel zwischen echter und künstlicher Intelligenz. 
 
Im Fokus der Gespräche stand daher, wie eng Finanzpolitik, technologische Entwicklung und Beschäftigung miteinander verbunden sind. Investitionen in Infrastruktur – wie zuletzt in die KI-Fabrik in München – sind zweifelsohne eine wichtige Grundlage. Entscheidend ist jedoch, ob wir Anwender bleiben oder den Anspruch entwickeln, Weltmarktführer für KI-gestützte Geschäftsmodelle zu werden – und ob wir KI dabei konsequent menschenzentriert denken. 
 
Dafür braucht es die Mitarbeitenden aller Unternehmen, die sich in der Allianz der Chancen zusammengeschlossen haben. KI und Mensch müssen dabei Hand in Hand gehen. Auch in dem Bewusstsein, die richtige Tonalität zu treffen, um auf die Ängste vieler Menschen zu reagieren. Mein Eindruck ist, dass wir uns bei Unsicherheit oftmals wieder an alten Verhaltensmustern bedienen, die wir eigentlich schon geglaubt, überwunden zu haben. Hier wünsche ich mir ein gemeinsames Narrativ, eine gemeinsame Strategie aus Politik und Wirtschaft. 
  
Ein herzliches Dankeschön an Ulrike Zeiler für die Gastfreundschaft im Allianz-Forum, an Vizekanzler und Bundesminister Lars Klingbeil für den Impuls, an Dr. Ariane Reinhart für die Moderation und an alle Teilnehmenden für den offenen Austausch und die inspirierenden Perspektiven. So leisten Formate wie die Allianz der Chancen einen wichtigen Beitrag für die Arbeitswelt von morgen.

The way AI is shaped will shape the world!
 
The question therefore is: Do we want to remove biases or reinforce blind spots? One alarm signal for the latter is that various studies indicate only around 22-30% of global AI talent is female.
 
At RWE, however, we strive to do the former. We want AI in our organisation to reflect the perspectives, creativity, and empathy of everyone – not just a few. This week I had the pleasure of joining the launch event for our Women in AI network. The network brings together women from different functions across teams and countries, creating a space to connect, learn, and experiment. It’s about more than representation – it’s about enabling women to actively and responsibly shape AI in ethical, inclusive ways.
 
During the discussion I shared my view of AI as a key enabler of digital transformation and the energy transition. And about what is needed in terms of a strong foundation for AI to scale. It's what I call a golden triangle consisting of:
▪️HR – to bring purpose and heart
▪️IT – to drive innovation
▪️Security – to provide the trust that allows us to move fast without breaking things
 
Together, they form the foundation of an organisation where AI can act as a co-pilot, supporting employees and freeing up time for creative, strategic work by humans. This is where women make a real difference. Uncertainty is no longer the exception, it’s now part of leadership.
 
How do uncertainty and a rapidly changing world shape the way we lead? This was a topic in the panel discussion with Colette Rückert-Hennen we had at  The London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE) German Symposium.
 
From my personal perspective – being responsible for HR, IT and Security – the challenge is even more fundamental: We are moving from an era of efficiency to an era of agency. The past decades, leadership was about managing “Human Resources”. Now, AI is finally taking the 'robot' out of the job. It is absorbing the management chores, the data-drudgery, and the administrative friction. This creates spaces. New possibilities. 

The big question for us on this panel is: What would be the wisest way to fill the newly created spaces? Our shared conviction: If we manage to fill it with Human Agency - transparency, radical vulnerability, and shared leadership - we turn uncertainty into our greatest competitive advantage. My goal is to use technology as a multiplier, not a replacer, so that our collective time becomes our company’s most valuable asset.

Are women better prepared for uncertain times, as there is something called the "female" leadership style? 

I try to avoid stereotypes, but research shows that in times of high stress, there is the temptation to revert to autocratic styles when the world feels 'Brittle' or 'Incomprehensible' (BANI). It feels safe to have one person 'set the course.' But I have to argue the opposite. Autocracy is a bottleneck. In an era where AI agents are processing data and making micro-decisions in milliseconds, an autocratic leader becomes the slowest part of the system. An autocratic leader who pretends to have all the answers creates a fragile organisation. A leader who shows vulnerability and transparency creates a resilient one. In a BANI world, collaboration is a survival skill, not a 'soft' skill. And so is Diversity!

Thanks to Hartmann Ilka for your moderation, and again to Colette Rückert-Hennen. It’s always a pleasure to share perspectives and the stage with you.
 
Actually, this thoroughly inspiring day began already in the morning with a meeting at the German Embassy in London where we had the opportunity to speak with the British Ambassador, H.E. Andrew Mitchell, and the German Ambassador, H.E. Susanne Baumann. This exchange provided valuable international perspectives on leadership as well. A day fully packed with great discussions.

Let's start the year with a view!
 
After taking you on a virtual tour of a wind turbine, today we're heading to the “heart” of the offshore wind farm: the substation.
 
What you see here is the offshore substation of our Kaskasi wind farm, 35 km off the coast of Heligoland. The substation is the central hub where electricity from all turbines comes together before heading to shore. From the outside, it might seem like just another platform at sea, but inside it’s a giant tangle of components and connections, all designed to make the flow of electricity reliable and continuous.
 
What kind of work goes into this heart of an offshore wind farm? Nothing less than an engineering masterpiece in manufacturing, heavy-lift vessels to transport the thousands of tonnes of topside components, and absolute precision during the “marriage” at sea – the installation of the topside onto the foundation. 
 
Once completed, the wind turbines turn, the generators produce electricity, and this is fed into the relevant grid connections via the substation. Sounds simple – but take a look for yourself! It’s easy to forget, from the outside, just how much care and coordination goes into making everything work. 
 
Looking ahead, RWE Offshore Wind will deliver four construction projects with a total capacity of 4.8 GW and continue providing clean, reliable electricity from our wind farms. Considering the dedication that goes into every detail, it’s clear that none of this would be possible without #TeamRWE.

Using AI, the researchers analysed more than 250,000 scientific publications and identified 31 key factors grouped into five dimensions: 
 
• Leadership and governance 
• Culture and collaboration 
• Resources and intellectual property 
• Technology and data 
• Ecosystems and markets 
 
The message is clear: technology is only one part of the picture. Human connection, learning and trust turn transformation into lasting progress.

Transformation requires collaboration and new approaches 🤝 
 
Network meetings like the 5-year anniversary of the #AllianzDerChancen – a network of companies and institutions that collaborates to actively shape the transformation of the labor market – are a strong reminder of how essential a constructive dialogue between business, academia and policymakers is. Especially in times of profound transformation. As Daimler Truck AG, we are a member of this alliance.
 
I leave the discussions with three key takeaways: 
 
- Transformation can only be successful if it includes labor market perspectives 
- Up- and re-skilling are crucial for competitiveness  
- Personnel platforms can be a meaningful instrument for enhancing cooperation 
 
 Transformation succeeds when stakeholders work together on solutions – turning ideas into action.

Empowering People, Driving the Future: Our New Truck Training Center in Poland 🚚

Recently, we proudly opened our brand-new Truck Training Center in Nadarzyn, Poland — a true milestone in how we at Daimler Truck AG invest in our people and their development to strengthen our whole business ecosystem. 
 
Spanning around 700 square meters, the center is designed to provide hands-on, practical training for our sales and service teams, with dedicated spaces for theoretical lessons, e-learning, and service workshops. In addition to that, we’re also welcoming bodybuilders, drivers, and customers who want to deepen their knowledge and skills. 
 
What excites me most is the focus on continuous learning and future-ready expertise, especially around electric mobility.
 
At the opening, we handed over 75 brand-new Mercedes-Benz Actros L ProCabin trucks to our Polish dealer network. 
 
Here’s to building knowledge, empowering teams, and moving forward — together.

Throughout my career, I have seen what a powerful lever for growth mentoring can be, both as a mentee and as a mentor. It fosters personal development, drives knowledge exchange, and strengthens your network.

The most important questions rarely have simple answers.
 
Palm oil is a good example. It is one of the most discussed raw materials in the world, yet the conversation is often framed as either good or bad. The reality is more nuanced.
 
Palm (kernel) oil is an important ingredient in many everyday products and its impact depends largely on how it is produced and sourced. At Henkel, we are committed to achieving zero net deforestation for palm (kernel) oil by 2030. Together with our suppliers and partners, we work to increase transparency and traceability across the supply chain, protect forests and natural ecosystems, and support the transition towards more sustainable production. This helps protect primary forests and improve the livelihoods of smallholder farmers.
 
The last aspect is often overlooked: understanding the people behind the supply chain, the challenges they face, and how responsible sourcing can improve their lives.
 
That’s why we have been partnering with Solidaridad Network since 2013 to support smallholder farmers through sustainable agricultural practices, certification processes and digital solutions that increase transparency.
 
Because meaningful progress happens when environmental and social considerations are addressed together.
 
#WeAreHenkel

Developing AI capabilities in our teams is just as important as investing in technology itself.
 
I recently came together with the HR Leadership Team to pilot a new AI leadership program before rolling it out more broadly across Henkel. Co-designed and delivered with our long-standing partner, IESE Business School, the program explored the strategic impact of AI on business, leadership, decision-making, and the future of work.
 
As leaders, we have a responsibility to understand the fundamental transformation driven by AI and help shape it. And that requires upskilling. Because it is not just about understanding the technology itself. Adopting an AI-first mindset has several dimensions:
 
1.    From us as individuals, it requires curiosity and an honest self-reflection on our willingness and ability to experiment.
2.    As leaders, we need to be ready to challenge established ways of working, rethink roles and responsibilities and compose future-ready teams.
3.    And to help our teams navigate this change ethically and with confidence, we need strong governance and clear rules.
 
No matter how much experience we have, leadership in the age of AI requires a sense of urgency – and a learner’s mindset.
 
#WeAreHenkel

Real progress is shaped by the decisions we make every day.
 
Spending time with our logistics teams on the Düsseldorf campus at Henkel again broadened my perspective on how much thoughtful experimentation goes into something we often take for granted: moving people and goods in a more sustainable way.
 
I was impressed by the progress already achieved. Nearly 40% of our 1,300 company cars in Germany are already fully electric – and that share will continue to grow with every newly ordered vehicle. In our headquarters truck fleet, none of the vehicles run on conventional diesel: around 80% of all kilometres are driven using HVO100, reducing CO₂ emissions by approximately 80%, while another 20% are covered by electric trucks.
 
It’s about the mindset behind these numbers. When the market didn’t yet offer the right solution, the team worked with partners to develop its own electric shunting vehicle – and is already working on the next one.
 
That’s the mindset we need. Not waiting for perfect conditions, but taking initiative, experimenting, and continuously improving. Sustainable transformation happens through many small but concrete decision – driven by people who are willing to rethink how things are done.
 
#WeAreHenkel

You can only manage what you can measure, especially in sustainability.
 
Measuring environmental impact can be more complex than traditional business metrics, with incomplete data and evolving standards. That’s why at Henkel, we’ve spent years building a strong data foundation – which is the basis for the road ahead, with concrete sustainability targets coming soon.
 
Across our Henkel Consumer Brands portfolio, a three-year analysis now gives us clear insights into product carbon footprints, and where transformation is needed – what meets our sustainability criteria, what needs to be redesigned. 
 
In Henkel Adhesive Technologies, our HEART (Henkel Environmental Assessment Reporting) tool calculates the footprint of more than 70,000 products, creating transparency for our customers and helping us steer our portfolio toward lower-emission solutions. Why does this matter? For industries like automotive, where we contribute to Scope 3 emissions, reliable data is essential for our customers to meet their climate goals.
 
Building these data capabilities requires collaboration with suppliers worldwide. I’m not tired of saying this: we can only make real progress if we work hand in hand across the value chain. 
 
With thanks to Bertrand Conquéret, Ulla Hueppe and Agnès Thée for driving this work forward.

What inspires me most about AI is not what it can do on its own, but how it can expand what we’re capable of as humans.

If we only use AI to do what we’ve always done – just faster and cheaper – we miss the bigger opportunity. Used well, AI can challenge our thinking, spark new ideas, and push us to ask better questions – just like a valuable sparrings partner or companion. It doesn’t replace human judgment – it amplifies it. 
 
As a global company and employer, we have a big responsibility: to take our people with us on this fast-moving journey. Here’s how we approach it at Henkel: 
  
🔹 We build AI literacy at scale.
From company-wide learning programs to leadership training, we want everyone to understand how AI can support their work (not replace it).
 
 🔹 We encourage our teams to experiment.
Across HR and the business, teams are already exploring how AI can help them work differently and better. This bottom-up energy is powerful.
 
 🔹 We keep people at the center.
Critical thinking, creativity, and empathy remain uniquely human. AI amplifies these strengths.
 
The future of work will not be defined by technology alone. It will be defined by how we choose to use it. 
 
I’m curious – what role does AI already play in your own learning or growth journey?

Two years ago, we took a bold step at Henkel: introducing 8 weeks of fully paid parental leave for all new parents – regardless of gender, family constellation, or location – across all ~70 countries and for all 47,000 colleagues.
 
We were the first company in the German DAX to do this.
We knew it would be complex. But we knew it was the right thing to do – and that it would make us stronger, as a company, as a team.
 
Today, the results from last year speak for themselves. And honestly, they move me.
 
📈 +15% overall uptake vs. 2024
 👨‍👩‍👧 +35% more male colleagues taking parental leave
 
In some countries, this is normal. In others, it’s a radical change. One story from a country in the Middle East region really stayed with me: in 2024, not a single father took parental leave. Last year, 84 male colleagues did.
 
I’m convinced this also pays off for Henkel: attracting talent, enhancing benefits, boosting employee satisfaction and retention – and the numbers prove it. But it’s more than metrics. It shows that companies can spark societal change. More equity. More shared responsibility. More equality in caregiving. #WeAreHenkel

“Only if everybody – young and old – is able to learn can we solve global challenges together. A rapidly developing world does not allow for learning to finish with the end of compulsory or higher education.” – UNESCO Institute for Lifelong Learning
 
This thought captures exactly why the International Day of Education matters so much to me.
 
We are living in a time of profound change – technological, societal, and environmental. In moments like these, learning becomes more than acquiring new skills: it helps us stay curious instead of fearful, critical instead of polarized, and open instead of certain that we already have all the answers.
 
Education supports our ability to think critically, understand different perspectives, and engage in meaningful dialogue. These aspects are essential foundations for strong and democratic societies. Especially when the world feels complex or uncertain, lifelong learning allows people to stay connected, informed, and able to shape change responsibly.
 
What we should not forget: in some countries, education is not a given. It is a luxury that many cannot afford. I had the privilege of growing up in a country that guarantees free education, and this is what allowed me to be where I am today. And I experienced the opportunity to receive higher education as a life-changer.
 
It is our all responsibility to make sure that we take all people with us. That everyone has the chance to receive education and shape their own future.
 
Organizations also have a key role to play in this. Creating environments where upskilling and exchange are encouraged helps people grow, not only professionally, but also as active members of society. And by offering young people the opportunity to enter the job market – keeping on learning beyond.
 
At Henkel, we strive to make learning a natural part of everyday work, across generations, regions, roles, and stages of life.
 
I would like to thank everyone who learns, teaches, mentors, and shares knowledge, helping keep curiosity and dialogue alive.
 
What’s something you have learned recently that made you see the world differently?

2025. What a year! A year of persistent geopolitical tensions and sweeping change. Of breathtaking technological leaps. Of challenges – and opportunities.

For us at Henkel, 2025 was about moving forward together. Let me share some highlights of our journey:

-  We worked hand-in-hand with our businesses to guide transformation and change, and we integrated new teams from our recent acquisitions.

-  We accelerated HR digitalization as we continued to unify our core HR systems into the cloud, with trusted partners at our side.

-  And I also visited teams across our regions and took part in key conferences – moments that gave me fresh insights and honest conversations about the challenges and opportunities we share, in HR and in Sustainability.
 
Looking ahead to 2026, our priorities remain clear:
-  Shape and support transformation end‑to‑end.
-  Build a future‑ready workforce where everyone can learn and thrive.
-  Continue our culture journey: embrace change with a growth mindset, and make Diversity, Equity & Inclusion central to how we lead.
-  Strengthen our strategy for digitalization and prepare for future AI-driven solutions.
-  Progress towards our net-zero targets with teamwork and dedication.
 
On a personal note: I’m genuinely optimistic for us as a team! We have a clear plan and most importantly we have great people. I see their passion, resilience and dedication. I’ve had countless conversations this year that remined we why I love my job and our Henkel spirit!

134 years. That’s how long it could take to close the global gender gap at the current pace, according to the World Economic Forum.

At Beiersdorf, we made a conscious decision years ago: we want to be as diverse as the consumers and communities we serve.

Back then in 2017, women held only 28.8% of top management roles, and our Executive Board was entirely male. As a team, we listened carefully and challenged our assumptions to rethink what needs to be true to change that - and reach gender parity. 

Four levers became central to this journey
💙 ensuring fairness in how we hire and promote 
💙 strengthening our internal talent pipelines 
💙 fostering inclusive leadership globally
💙 and embedding flexibility into career paths – for example, through jobsharing (a game changer!)

The result: in 2023, we reached gender parity across all global management levels, including our Executive and Supervisory Boards. And we’ve sustained it since.

I’m very proud of our progress but we can only scale when we share and build on what works. That’s why exchange with others matters. And today I had one of these opportunities: a group of leaders from the “A Seat at the Table” initiative by manager magazin visited us to exchange about our gender parity journey.

Thank you to Simone, and to all participants, for the open dialogue. And to our colleagues Misel, Christina, Birte and Kibreab for bringing this topic to life by sharing your insights and jobsharing experiences.

#Beiersdorf #GenderParity #aSEATatthetable #TOP100

My Daily Question: “Am I a Good Leader?”

Reflection has become one of the most powerful tools in my leadership journey. Every evening on my way home, I ask myself one simple question:
Was I a good leader today?

Not perfect. Just present. 
Did I listen enough? 
Did I create clarity? 
Did I create an environment where others can thrive?
Did I make someone feel valued?

This small ritual keeps me grounded. It reminds me that leadership is a responsibility that shows in the smallest moments. 

Some days, the answer feels like a yes. 
Other days, I see room to grow and to be very honest, I am not happy with myself. 
And that’s okay because leadership is a journey, not a destination.

This practice becomes even more valuable in moments of change when things are moving fast, staying centered matters most and it’s easy to lose sight of the small actions that shape how we show up.

You can’t force productivity. You build it through environments where people feel trusted, valued, and empowered.

During my keynote at Mercer’s Human Works Conference themed "All eyes on productivity", I shared how HR is taking the lead as a strategic co-pilot to create environments that help people thrive and, in turn, drive productivity. When designing the employee experience at Beiersdorf, I always return to three beliefs that anchor how we bring our purpose to life.

1️⃣ 𝗔𝘀 𝗱𝗶𝘃𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗲 𝗮𝘀 𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘀𝘂𝗺𝗲𝗿𝘀
To truly build an inclusive culture, you need both mindset and action: leaders who understand inclusion and systems that make it real. We reached global gender parity among our leaders in 2023, continue to advance disability inclusion through, for instance, our employee community “Ability” and have embarked on a major journey to upskill all 3,000+ people leaders through our three-month DEI Essentials program with around 70% already finished.

2️⃣ 𝗢𝘂𝘁𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝗵𝗮𝗽𝗽𝗲𝗻𝘀 𝘄𝗵𝗲𝗻 𝗲𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗼𝘆𝗲𝗲𝘀 𝗰𝗮𝗻 𝗯𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗶𝗿 𝗯𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝘀𝗲𝗹𝗳
Enabling everyone to be their best self means giving people the flexibility and security they need to thrive at work and beyond. That’s why we offer flexible working models, including 42 job-sharing tandems (over half in leadership roles), and support our employees in the Moments that Matter through our Global Critical Illness Policy, which provides paid leave, job security, and care for those facing life’s toughest challenges, whether personally or as caregivers.

3️⃣ 𝗪𝗲 𝗯𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗲𝘃𝗲 𝗶𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗽𝗼𝘄𝗲𝗿 𝗼𝗳 𝘄𝗲
One of the clearest examples of how care connects people, builds pride, and strengthens engagement across our company is our global Care Beyond Skin Day. Every year, more than 10,000 colleagues across 65 countries dedicate over 60,000 hours to local volunteering projects giving their time, skills, and heart. Our internal research confirms what we feel: 72% of participants say the experience makes them feel more engaged and connected to Beiersdorf

In the end, it’s simple: when people feel seen, valued, and empowered they bring their best selves to work and that’s what drives real productivity. Our role as senior leaders is getting the balance right between raising the bar for performance in an increasingly more difficult environment while strengthening a culture where everyone can thrive. If these two go together, we can unlock productivity.

The closer we stay to our people, the better we lead

Staying in touch with our people is one of the most important parts of my role. That’s why I make it a priority to be approachable and to regularly connect with colleagues across all levels – to listen, to learn, and to exchange perspectives. Our Lunch Connect format in HR is a wonderful opportunity to spend valuable time with colleagues across the organization.

Whether it’s a town hall, a team meeting, or just a chat in the coffee kitchen, every conversation helps me understand what matters most to our colleagues. It’s my daily dose of learning, inspiration, and connection.

Our recent HR Lunch Connect was another great example of how powerful these informal moments can be. We talked about career journeys, our own modernization, the importance of learning and what is next on the agenda.  Every time I walk away with new ideas and a deeper appreciation for the passion and purpose that drive our people.

A big thank you to Talita Queiroz Alves, Gloria S., Anna Nina Börner, and Elisa Maehl for such an open, inspiring conversation and for your honesty, passion, and great ideas! I learned a lot from you!

The team in Poland was among the first to go live with our new HR operating model. Transformation is rarely a simple lift & shift. It takes courage, collaboration, and a willingness to move forward even when things aren’t perfect. As my dear colleague Astrid wisely says: “If you wait until everything is perfect, you’ve been waiting too long.”

I’m incredibly proud of how far we’ve come and deeply grateful for the passion, energy, and drive of our team in Poland. A heartfelt thank you to, Sandra Hefenbrock Agata Walczykiewicz-Węgiel, Agnieszka Idczak-Stysiak, Karolina Serafin, and all our wonderful HR colleagues – as well as Frank Janssen, Aleksander Olszewski, and Dr. Martin Stoebe – for your great support and ambassadorship along the way!

This serum is the first based on epigenetic science. It features our breakthrough ingredient EPICELLINE®, which we developed through 15 years of research and scientifically proven to reverse skin aging and activating skin longevity. 💙

Last weekend, Beiersdorf stood proudly at the heart of 🌈 CSD Hamburg. Over 250 colleagues came together to show what inclusion means in action: demonstrating, dancing, and standing up for the right to be who we are — without fear, without compromise but with joy and love.

Thank you to our fantastic Be You Community, our dedicated Event Management team, and everyone behind the scenes who made this possible. You reminded us all: inclusion doesn’t happen by accident. It happens because people CARE to make it visible. ❤️🧡💛💚🩵💜🤎🖤

Masayuki Imagawa joined Takeda Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. in 2008 and quickly established himself as a leader in strategic business planning and global project implementation. In 2012, Masayuki co-founded Takeda’s Vaccine Business Division, laying the foundation for its future success. Over the following decade, Masayuki led impactful programs, including a major milestone in 2020 for Takeda’s COVID-19 vaccine program, securing critical government funding for two vaccine candidates. His leadership also contributed to the NDA approvals for H5N1 pandemic flu vaccines, advancing pandemic preparedness. Masayuki’s strategic vision culminated in the successful launch of mRNA and recombinant protein COVID-19 vaccines in Japan through collaborations with Moderna and Novavax, earning him the Takeda Executive Team Award in 2022 for significant contributions to the Spikevax project. As a recognized leader in pandemic preparedness, Masayuki frequently addressed public forums over the last three years, highlighting his expertise in vaccine strategy and implementation. His first year leading the Vaccine Business Unit under Takeda Japan Pharma Business Unit (FY2022) was exceptionally successful, delivering outstanding public health and business outcomes through FY2024. In FY2025, Masayuki began his new role as Vice President, Head of Vaccine Division in Business Unit I, JPBU, furthering his impact on Takeda’s global mission. Prior to joining Takeda, Masayuki accrued over 14 years of experience in Japan and the EU with Ono Pharmaceutical Co., where he honed his global perspective. His tenure at Ono was marked by high recognition, including the CEO Award and the Ono Brightest Scientist Award. Beyond Takeda, Masayuki has held several key external leadership and advisory positions, including: Chief Executive of the Japanese Association of Vaccine Industries and Member of the Board of Directors for the Vaccination Research Center (until 2024). A generic landing page does not automatically mean an AI slop website.

Yes, we’ve all seen the familiar patterns:
1. Big headline.
2. Purple gradient.
3. Bento-grid features.
4. “Revolutionize your workflow with AI.”

They can make a website feel generic but visual similarity alone tells us very little about the actual product.

A templated landing page can still lead to a useful, reliable product that solves a real problem. Meanwhile, a beautifully designed and completely original website can still hide broken features, fake testimonials, and little real value.

The better question is not:
“Does this website look AI-generated?”

It is:
“If we remove the polished visuals, does this product still provide meaningful value to a specific user?”

AI-assisted development is not the problem. The problem begins when generated output is treated as the finished product without enough judgment, testing, originality, or understanding of the user.

Generic design is a branding problem.

AI slop is a substance problem.

Store vs Warehouse vs Logistics: What Is the Difference?
Many people think Store, Warehouse, and Logistics mean the same thing, but they are completely different functions in the supply chain. Understanding these differences is essential for anyone working in inventory, warehouse operations, or logistics.

 📦 Store vs Warehouse vs Logistics – Do You Know the Difference?
Many people use these three terms interchangeably, but each has a unique role in the supply chain.
🔹 Store – Ensures materials are available for daily operations. Its focus is stock availability and issuing materials when needed.
🔹 Warehouse – Manages inventory efficiently through receiving, storage, picking, packing, and dispatch while maintaining high inventory accuracy.
🔹 Logistics – Connects the entire supply chain by transporting goods from suppliers to warehouses and finally to customers—on time and at the lowest possible cost.
From my 10+ years of experience in warehouse operations, I've learned that supply chain success doesn't depend on just one function. It depends on how well Store, Warehouse, and Logistics work together.
✅ Store keeps operations running.
✅ Warehouse keeps inventory under control.
✅ Logistics keeps business moving.
When these three functions are aligned, businesses achieve higher productivity, lower costs, and better customer satisfaction.
